description: Summary The Wikimedia Foundation is looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer to join our team, reporting to the Sr. Engineering Manager. As the Site Reliability Engineer, you will play a key role in designing, developing, and maintaining reliable, scalable, and highly available infrastructure for our API services. You will contribute heavily to the high impact challenges behind innovating, building, and maintaining Wikipedia’s data feeds for high volume reusers. In this role, you will foster cross department collaboration with the wikimedia foundation SRE teams. You will own reliability targets (SLOs) for critical APIs, balancing performance, cost, and availability through data-driven decisions. You will be involved in designing and running the infrastructure and services that interact with the base of Wikimedia Foundation’s projects, including, but not limited to: Kubernetes clusters, application servers, code collaboration infrastructure, and  other developer-facing services. You will participate in incident response and be on-call. This role requires frequent work with other members of the enterprise and Foundation SRE team to maintain and improve our systems, as well as interacting with people not in SRE, like Security, Release and Software Engineers, together striving to move our projects and technologies forward.  Wikimedia Enterprise is a new, revenue-generating product that provides fast, comprehensive, reliable, and secure data ingestion for organizations that wish to repurpose Wikimedia/Wikipedia content in third party environments. Wikimedia Enterprise aims to improve the user experience for Wikimedia/Wikipedia readers beyond our own websites; increase the reach and discoverability of Wikimedia/Wikipedia content; and improve awareness and ease of attribution and verifiability of Wikimedia/Wikipedia content by the organizations that reuse our content the most. You can learn more about the project in WIRED and Insider . We are a distributed and diverse team of engineers with a drive to explore, experiment, and embrace  technologies. We act sort of like a startup within the Wikimedia Foundation: we build quickly, deploy often, and our work has a very high impact on the global knowledge ecosystem. If you are up to the challenge of working on something fast paced, of creating services that will revolutionize the systems distributing our knowledge for billions of people across the world, and enjoy the idea of working with a globally distributed team, you might be just the person we need.  You are responsible for: Define, track, and improve Service Level Objectives (SLOs), SLIs, and error budgets to ensure reliability targets are met Build and enhance observability systems (metrics, logs, and distributed tracing) to enable proactive detection and faster troubleshooting Drive reliability engineering practices, including capacity planning, load testing, and resilience validation (e.g., chaos testing) Improve developer experience (DevEx) by enabling self-service infrastructure and streamlining deployment workflows Partner with engineering team members to embed reliability best practices early in the development lifecycle  Design, implement, and optimize CI/CD and GitOps workflows using tools such as GitLab (or similar) and ArgoCD(or similar), enabling automated, reliable deployments with support for progressive delivery strategies like canary and blue-green releases Implement secure-by-default infrastructure and enforce best practices (e.g., IAM, secrets management, encryption) Continuously optimize infrastructure cost and efficiency using FinOps principles while maintaining performance and availability Establish and track operational metrics such as MTTR, MTTD, and incident frequency to drive continuous improvement Reduce operational toil by identifying repetitive work and implementing automation-first solutions Contribute to and evolve internal platform capabilities that standardize infrastructure and improve scalability across teams Collaborating with a global and asynchronously communicating team (don’t worry if you have never worked remotely, we’ll help you get used to it) Mentoring peers in your areas of technical and operational strength Skills and Experience: Automation & Configuration Management: Experience with Infrastructure as Code and automation tools (e.g., Terraform, Ansible) and proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Go, or similar) Cloud Infrastructure: Experience designing, operating, and optimizing cloud-based systems across platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, including scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency CI/CD & Deployment Practices: Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows (e.g., GitLab or similar, ArgoCD), with familiarity in progressive delivery approaches such as canary and blue-green deployments Incident Management & Reliability Operations: Experience with incident response, on-call practices, and leading postmortems, with a focus on continuous improvement and operational excellence SRE Principles & Observability: Strong understanding of SRE best practices, including SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets, along with experience in observability (metrics, logging, and distributed tracing e.g., Prometheus, OpenTelemetry) Collaboration & Communication: Ability to work effectively in a distributed, cross-functional environment, with strong documentation and communication skills Familiarity with Wikimedia or other open source projects is a plus. description: PRINCIPAL, GLOBAL EVENT SECURITY AND RISK MANAGEMENT Summary The Wikimedia Foundation is looking for a Principal, Global Event Security and Risk Management, to join our team. Our aim is to ensure everyone, everywhere can securely participate in free knowledge. As an organization, we are committed to proactively identifying and mitigating risks that impact both the Foundation and the Wikimedia movement. This includes enabling secure physical convenings and spaces for the robust global communities of volunteers we serve and often support through grants, and effectively addressing other physical security and enterprise risks our ecosystem faces. The Principal will report to the Deputy General Counsel in the Legal Department, and will lead the Foundation’s efforts in proactively preparing for and addressing critical risks to the physical security of staff, community members, and other participants engaging in Wikimedia movement activities. The Principal will coordinate with staff in the Foundation’s internal Enterprise Risk Management working group to broadly identify and track risks to the Foundation and Wikimedia movement. In their focused work of identifying and leading the response to physical security threats, the Principal will partner with internal teams such as legal, grantmaking, external and movement communications, human rights, product security, and trust & safety; and groups outside of the Foundation, such as Wikimedia volunteer organizers, external partners, and security experts.   As the point person for the mitigation of physical security risks, the Principal must remain informed on global geopolitical developments, in order to identify emerging and shifting threats to Wikimedia users around the world, and synthesize information from a variety of sources, including Foundation risk reports and consultations with internal teams. The Principal’s goal is to support the organization, the Wikimedia movement and its communities in their efforts to reduce vulnerability and minimize harm when threats materialize. The successful candidate will possess a wide range of experience and a deep understanding of best practices in risk coordination and response, security, and crisis management. They will have experience working in global contexts, particularly the global south, and will bring curiosity, an ability to work across different cultures, and vision. They will have strong people skills, with the ability to empathetically motivate and inspire both staff and volunteers, while understanding the needs and capacities of disparate stakeholder groups. Their experience and good judgment will enable them to achieve impact on a wide variety of high-stakes, emergent risk issues facing the Foundation and the communities it supports.   You are responsible for: Working closely with Wikimedia movement organizers to develop and maintain an understanding of the environments and challenges facing Wikimedia volunteers around the world, mitigate those risks, and define best practices for physical security in movement activities. Strengthening the Foundation’s overall enterprise risk management approach and execution, including policy development and implementation. Leading the process to create risk and gap assessments, to identify, document, and track high risks for the Foundation, consulting with subject matter experts in technology, brand, operational, legal, and strategic risk. Improving the organization’s expertise in identifying, mitigating against, and addressing emerging physical security threats to Wikimedia’s staff, communities, and affiliated organizations.  Leading risk assessments for community conferences and other events funded by the Foundation, including consolidating input from multiple teams, and communicating the findings to various stakeholders, including community organisers. Creating emergency response plans for physical security threats, bringing together stakeholders and experts as necessary from the organization, law enforcement agencies, or external consultants where appropriate, and managing the implementation of those plans once approved.   Being on-call as required to review emergency alerts to ensure proper escalation of and response to physical security threats, including leading emergency response working groups during an emergent situation, designating an on-site incident coordinator as needed, and providing risk management expertise. Remaining current on emerging geopolitical trends and best practices in physical security. Briefing the Deputy General Counsel and senior leadership on a regular basis, with recommendations about what works, what doesn’t, and financial and staff resource management, focused on ongoing systems improvement. Providing crisis support to other internal teams who work directly with at-risk communities. Skills and Experience: Substantial professional experience in corporate and physical security work in a variety of geographic and political contexts. It is particularly valuable to have experience working in the global south. Substantial risk management experience, particularly experience in a leadership role that involved risk management.  Substantial experience developing, communicating, and executing emergency response plans.  Strong networking and analytical skills, with the ability to process and synthesize large amounts of information on geopolitical trends and elucidate their specific impact on the organization and its stakeholders.
